batting.name: S Dube
batting.dismissal: c M Shahrukh Khan b Arshdeep Singh

batting.name: MM Ali
batting.dismissal: st JM Sharma b RD Chahar

batting.name: RA Jadeja
batting.dismissal: c LS Livingstone b SM Curran

batting.name: P Simran Singh
batting.dismissal: st MS Dhoni b RA Jadeja

batting.name: S Dhawan
batting.dismissal: c M Pathirana b TU Deshpande

batting.name: LS Livingstone
batting.dismissal: c RD Gaikwad b TU Deshpande

batting.name: JM Sharma
batting.dismissal: c SK Rasheed b TU Deshpande

balls.text: make it two to make it an even 200. Dhoni's philosophy: don't try too much, but maximise if the bowler errs. Curran errs by missing his yorker. Bowls a low full toss, and he smacks it way over deep midwicket for a 88m six
he bowls a wide bouncer, trying ti keep it away from Dhoni, but he upper-cuts it over point. Just gets enough to clear the boundary. Dhoni has given his fans what they wanted

falls just short of deep midwicket. We are still confirming it with the third umpire. Slower short ball, pulled in the air, doesn't get all of it, Livingstone has to run to his right and also come in. He puts the dive in, and jams his finger in the ground as he goes for it. The ball is stuck in just two fingers. He might just have got them under the ball, you know. No he hasn't. This can't be given out. There won't be a century for Conway
slower wide ball, but he has gone too wide
misses his yorker, but Dhoni ends up hitting this full ball straight to long-on for one
slower ball, short of a length, Dhoni tries to get inside the line and pull it over short wide. Beaten. The roar finally settles down

Jadeja's strange innings comes to an end. No boundary intent so far, and when he tries to hit this leg-stump full toss for six, he ends up mis-hitting it straight to deep midwicket. On this pitch, Jadeja will have a lot to say with the ball, though

again a slower ball, 123ks, but Conway this time manages to hit this lofted drive straight of long-on for four. The only boundary in the last two overs. Conway in the 90s now. This is his highest score in the IPL
anther slower ball, on a length, wide outside off, Conway looks to late-cut it but is beaten
slower short ball, 115ks, pulled down to deep midwicket for one
slower ball again, 121ks, on a length, drilled straight to long-on for one
makes room, Rabada goes wide, concedes just the single to deep cover
slower ball, Conway tries to slog, gets an inside edge to short fine
looking for the ramp, Arshdeep goes wide with a slower one, and he ends up opening the face for a single to short third
down the wicket, gets too close to it, just the single to long-on
low full toss, and he has put it in the hole between long-on and deep midwicket for two more
slower ball, short of a length, 122ks, cramps him up and gets a bottom edge as he looks to open the face
gets the yorker right, dug out to long-on, and because it is going slowly, they steal the second
full and straight, put into a gap on the leg side
Chahar drags his length back, but Conway still sweeps him square on the leg side for four more
this is why he was shuffling across. Chahar has no one deep square on the leg side. He sweeps this full ball, and it is four all the way once it beats short fine to his right

Conway's premeditation has done himself in. He has shuffled across early to look to ramp/lap it, but he gets a juicy long hop legbreak, which he can't do anything with because of the position he finds himself in
on a length, legbreak, worked to square leg for one
wrong'un, short of a length, dropped into the leg side for a couple. Enough of a gap at deep midwicket
and he has a stumping. Moeen jumps out of the track, Chahar gets appreciable turn on a flat legbreak, it beats his slog on the inside, and he is gone
another slower legcutter, 112ks, short of a length, cut away hard, and puts it in the gap at point for a couple
gets away with it. A leg-stump yorker with no one deep square on the leg side. Flicked straight to square leg
slower legcutter bouncer, 117ks, but it is just a bit too wide on the off side
Rabada is unlucky. Conway opens the face on a wide yorker, Rabada puts in a full-length dive to his right at short third, gets a hand to it, but it still goes for four
another slower ball, this time short of a length, hit in the air but well short of deep cover for one
slower ball, Moeen delays the downswing of the bat, and crashes this over extra cover for four more
he gets away with a wide full toss. Point and third are both up. Moeen has timed the slice well, but he has hit it straight to point
tries to get out of the over with a wide yorker but ends up bowling a full toss. Conway drives it square for four more
flatter, on the stumps, pushed down to long-off
now Moeen goes over extra. Flatter than the Conway shot. More of a drive than a chip. But never does he try to hit a six. He is going for that four. Again gets the width
on a length, angling in, punched down to long-on for one
now he gets the short ball as a result of that last shot. Gets a couple straight of deep midwicket
lovely placement. Widish length ball, he knows he can't hit it for a six, and thus just chips it and goes over extra cover

slower ball does the trick. A wide slowie, on a length, Dube goes for it, tries to clear long-on, but ends up toe-ending it straight to long-on. Another ounce of muscle in this, and it would have cleared the man. Shows you how difficult it is for bowlers
yorker, dug out to cover-point for one
straight low full toss, hit straight to deep midwicket for one. Gets away with that one, does Arsh

slower ball, and Conway gets lucky. He has been done in completely, ends up skying it, and it drops right behind the bowler, just inside the 30-yard circle. He hasn't picked it because it is a knuckle ball
full and wide again, Dube drives the low full toss to long-off for one
tries to hide this wide, but bowls it too wide
misses the yorker, bowls a plum half-volley, and Dube drills it back over his head for four. That's now why he has been brought back
gets inside the line, and ramps this effortlessly. Fine leg is too square. How well has he picked his spots today?
this is the quicker short one, 146ks, at his hip, cramping him up, drawing the mis-hit, but he has mistimed it too much to carry to deep midwicket
another slower bouncer, but this one he has overcooked. Called a wide on height
slower bouncer this time, gets good height on it, Dube doesn't flirt with it
slower ball, tucked away off the hip for one
short of a length, pushed down to long-on for one
he is no good against pace, they said. Rabada goes short and fast. But this pitch doesn't have bounce. It is midriff high, and Dube has pulled it over midwicket for a six. Proper connection
full and quick, dug out back to Raza
tries another big mow to a full ball, gets a thick inside edge for a single
paddle sweep this time, straight to short fine, and gets a single
innovation from Conway. Goes down the reverse, gets a low fullie, and places it between backward point and short third. That brings up his fifty too
darted into the pads, and pushed into the leg side for one
Dube is not holding back. Raza has bowled short of a length, and he is quick to pull it over wide long-on for six
short, chest high, pulled down to deep forward square leg for one
on a length, middle and off, inside edge into the pad for one
slower ball, dug in shorter, pulled down to long-on for one
this time he gets some width, and Dube punches this square. Still can't beat backward point
short of a length, no room, helped to backward point
short of a length, tucked away off the hip for one
Dube into the act right away. Lofts this one back over his head. Doesn't get all of it, but he is going straight and there are no fielders there
misfielded at short extra cover. Again seems a bad bounce from the practice pitch. And he is fielding on that side strip. They get two for it

looks like the carrom ball. He has done him in completely. Oh no, it is a legbreak. It seems Gaikwad came down too early, and Raza had time to change his delivery, and also goes wide outside off. Gaikwad runs past it
straighter now, gets some turn, and Conway flicks it to deep midwicket for one
full, on off, and Conway goes hard and almost back over his head. Beats long-on to his right
goes roundarm again but overcooks it. Down the leg side, and Conway whips it past short fine for four
legbreak, just a bit of room, punched wide of long-off for two
legbreak, middle and leg, in-between length, played back to him
worked wide of midwicket for one
flatter, Conway goes back, pushes it to deep midwicket for one
down the wicket, and gives it a proper humpty. Don't think it is the best timing but there is enough muscle in it to clear long-on
down the wicket, beaten in the flight, gets a leg-bye
goes really roundarm. The spinning Malinga. Beats his outside edge
cut away straight to extra cover
quick offbreak, beats his attempt to run it down
lovely extra-cover drive. Jumps out of the crease, gets to its pitch, and creams it
offbreak, pushed to deep midwicket for one
on a length, no room, pushed back to him
quick legbreak, pushed to deep cover for one
tries the big slog sweep, but the legbreak turns in and takes the inside edge for a single
wrong'un, Conway goes backs and cuts, but can't beat the ring
nice drift, but not much turn, nudged into the leg side for one
flights one, overpitches, played along the ground to deep midwicket
on a length, legbreak, pushed towards long-on for one
on a length, tucked away off the pads for a single
misdirected down the leg side again, 109ks, and this time Gaikwad says he is not content with just the wide. He gets bat on it and beats short fine leg to his right
slower legcutter, massive drop in pace, 109sk, but well down leg
good height on this bouncer, pulled down to long leg for one
this is a bit of a shank as the length is shorter from the last time. A bit of a thick outside edge as he looks to go over mid-on. Still enough on it to clear the man
not the cleanest of hits. Looks to loft one from outside off, ends up dragging it towards mid-on, but he has got enough of a connection on it to clear the man inside the circle
full, on the pads, single to deep straight midwicket
is waiting for a flatter delivery but it sits in the surface and he gets just the single off the kinda bottom edge
third charge at him, and now he has got the right distance between himself and the pitch of the ball. Lofts him over long-on for a clean 96m six
short of a length, whipped to deep midwicket for one
gets the front edge on the reverse-sweep, ends up playing it to extra cover
down the wicket to push this to long-off for one
down the wicket, gets too close to the pitch of the ball, plays it to extra cover
full and straight, pushed down the ground, and Curran gets a hand to it to deny them a run
slower short ball, pulled to wide long-on for one. This one is bowled at 121ks
backs away to look to use the pace, 134ks too. Gaikwad opens the face but manages to find backward point
slower ball, short of a length, chopped down wide of backward point for one
full, driven hard but straight to mid-off
short of a length, tucked away off the hip for one
goes short, fine leg is up, and Conway pulls this down and square of the man. This is a quick start on a slow pitch
slower ball again, pushed straight to mid-on
slower ball, runs this to short third from where Rabada throws hard, and a bad bounce from a practice pitch for Brar, backing up, gives them the overthrow
pace on the ball, on a length, nowhere near driving length, but Gaikwad pushes it on the up, and finds the gap between mid-off and extra cover
slower ball, really full, driven straight to cover-point
over or around, if you bowl short and wide, Gaikwad won't show mercy. Square-cuts it through backward point for four
this is not slow, 143ks, and hits his thigh pad in a hurry as he looks to tuck this way to leg
picks the slower ball, 123ks, and he is down the pitch and making room to take this on the half-volley and drive it along the ground through cover
wide length ball, 138ks, good bounce, and Conway has gone up and over. A bit of a chip. He has got the room here, and goes over ccover-point
fuller, slower ball, 121ks, hits the inner half of the bat as Conway has a drive
lovely punch on the up, but straight to mid-off
on a length, angling in, beats the inside edge, goes for a leg-bye
another slower ball, pushed straight of short extra cover for a single
slight shimmy down the wicket, looks like a slower ball, pushed to backward point
bouncer, too high, and he ducks it. A wide

pushed across wider, and left alone this time. Hello, CSK want a wide and they have asked for the review. The replays show it is angling away, and it has gone above the guide line. CSK lose the review
on a length, going across, pushed to the left of that short point
overpitches just a bit, and Gaikwad leans on it to drive it through covers for four. No swing this time
this one swings back in, and cramps him up as he looks to open the face for a single
he starts way wide outside off. Slight shape away but the starting line is too wide

Raza has taken them home. What a superb final over from Pathirana. He goes slower ball into the surface, short of a length, outside off. Raza seems to have picked his spot. He moves across to pull it over square leg inside the circle. Bang in the middle of deep fine leg and deep midwicket. As you can imagine this slower ball has not been timed perfectly, but it keeps trickling away from square leg. Desperate fielding prevents the boundary but they take three runs
shuffles across early, drags the slower ball into the leg side, past square leg, gets two by the time Jadeja from deep midwicket fields and throws
full and straight, tries the big hit, goes off the inside half of the bat, straight of deep midwicket, gets two
slower ball, lovely slower ball, outside off, Raza is having a big slog at it, and the low bounce beats him
nails the inswinging yorker. Missing leg but another ball that just gets them one. That too a leg-bye n
full and wide, just the single to deep cover
short and wide, keeping the ball away from him, pulled to deep midwicket for one
qide outside off. Clearly outside the blue line even as he gets the yorker length right
wide full toss. Even though it has gone off the edge past short third for four, this one deserves punishment

has he touched the rope? Another slower ball, wide outside off, grips the surface, Jitesh looks to go straight, and toe-ends a skier towards long-on. Shaik Rasheed is the fielder who seems to have misjudged and come in too far. He goes back, takes it overhead and then trips. His back foot gets stuck and doesn't slip, which seems to have stopped it from hitting the boundary triangle. The third umpire takes a long look, and his reasoning for giving this out is "I don't see the board move". The other angle, I thought, showed him touch the triangle slightly, but I could be wrong. The third umpire is the expert here. He is not doing commentary while making the decision so we have to trust what he is seeing more than what I thought I saw
slower ball, just short of a length, beats him attempt to loft it down the ground from outside off
big wide outside off even though Jitesh has moved early. This is just too wide. Outside the return crease
again a low full toss, but not too wide. He opens the face on the drive, and gets two between deep third and deep cover
wide low full toss. I think he is going for the blue-line yorker, but overcooks it. Jitesh lofts it over extra cover for four. He is batting beautifully
full and wide, driven to deep cover for as single
kicks off a short of a length. Everything about his action says low bounce, but it grips the surface and jumps at his glove. SRK lucky it doesn't pop up
pinpoint yorker, on off, he gets the inside toe of the bat for a single
slower ball, short of a length, wide outside off, too wide outside off
Jitesh is playing like a dream. Again similar fullish roundarm delivery, he breaks his back knee to get low, and then just chips it over extra cover for four
full, on off, pushed to deep cover for one

oh this match is producing big plays after big plays. Again that natural inswing from that low angle beats the outside edge of Curran who things he has got a slot ball that he can loft back over his head. The off stumps is pegged back
on a length, middle and leg, dropped into the leg side for one more

another lovely shot. Down the wicket, also makes room to be able to swing at this, and whacks it straight back over his head for a six. Are people reminded of Jadeja's slow innings now, which began around this time in the first innings?
lovely shot. Jadeja bowls wicket to wicket, but Curran backs away to punch it past cover. Deshpande goes to his left from deep point and dives to save two runs
flat outside off, under edge for one as he looks to cut
Jitesh is an intent factory. Walks at a 102ks delivery from Jadeja, and slogs it clean over long-on for a 101m six. This is not over by a long way
on a length, no room, placed wide of short third for one
wide length ball, slower ball, runs this past backward point for two

oh he has pulled at a wide ball. You can't control them from this height. Deshpande has got this bouncer really high, Livingstone really just throws his bat at it, and deep midwicket takes a safe catch
short-ball offcutter, but this one doesn't grip in the surface. Livingstone pulls it over midwicket for six more. He is on fire here

again unfair on the bowler. Slower ball, 124ks, extra bounce, beats his swing, runs off the shoulder, Theekshana dives at short third and the ball bounces over him for four. No need to go for it really, but does Theekshana know it has come off the shoulder?
Livingstone is turning it on now. Gets a wide length ball, uses his reach to get under it, and lofts it over extra cover for six more. Game on
this is not fair. He has missed the yorker by mere inches, but Livingstone has somehow short-armed it over long-on for a flat six. That's great wrists
beaten. This is a full ball, in the slot, and Curran looks to go straight, but it turns past his edge and bounces over the stumps
Theekshana has got away with it. A full toss on the pads, but it is bowled at 106ks, and Livingstone is just a touch late on it. Shanks it to long-on
wide down the leg side, and a yorker to boot. Dhoni does well to get some body behind it, but they will run a bye
finally a boundary. Curran dances down, makes room, and drives it past extra cover all along the ground
thick outside edge as he looks to hit this half-volley over midwicket, but it turns even from that length. However, it doesn't carry to long-on and long-off
fires it into the toe as he sees him shuffle. Bowled at 105ks. Just the one leg-bye
carrom ball, wide outside off, but just inside the guide line. Livingstone can't make any connection
nearly a yorker, dug out for just the single to extra cover
misses out. Short ball, sits up to be hit, but he can't find the gap. Just the single to deep midwicket
bouncer, Curran knows mid-off is up so he goes down the ground with a flat bat and just about clears the diving Rahane
yorker on the toes, clipped to long leg for one
gets the width, looks to slash it, but the extra bounce beats him. Bowled at 143ks
slower ball, on a length, Livingstone ends up dragging it to deep square leg for two
down the wicket, gets too close to it, drives it hard into the ground, and it bounces over the bowler's head for a single
fired into the pads, pushed down to long-on for one
on a length, into the pads, put into the gap on the leg side for two
on a length, wide outside off, punched to deep cover for one
full, straight, offbreak, pushed to long-off for one
he is not expecting a full toss on the pads first ball, and pats it down to long-on for one

lovely shot and equally good fielding. Gets some width on this length ball, opens the face, places it past backward point, but Akash runs to his left from deep third and puts in a dive to save two runs
on a length, outside off, pushed to extra cover for one
Livingstone backs away this time, Pathirana follows him, and he smacks the pull for four through square leg
short of a length, low bounce, beats his outside edge as Livingstone looks to run it down with an open face
on a length, just outside off, runs it down to deep third for one
and you see immediately he is difficult to face. Full and driving length, but it swings away to beat his outside edge
slows it down, gets some turn, and Curran gets a single off the inside edge
on the pads, and Curran uses soft hands to take two in the leg side
he is running through his overs now. Pushed wide of him but Jadeja fields it to his right
full and straight, pushed back to him

Jadeja has fun after taking an easy catch. He just keeps bowling wide to Taide, who finally has a go at it and offers a straightforward return catch. Jadeja completes the catch, sees Livingstone is outside his crease, and then pretends to drop it to run him out instead. All for fun. Don't think Taide will be thrilled
pushed across him, and beats him on the drive. He needs to get a move on
low full toss, hit straight to mid-off for one
slower short ball. You could see Livingstone was looking for a huge pull. He checks the shot, and takes a single along the ground
Livingstone. Has. Arrived. Down the wicket, Akash goes short, and he has flat-batted a chest-high ball to wide long-off for a flat six
length ball, angling across, driven on the up, wide of mid-off, but not enough timing in it to get more than one
short of a length again, flicked towards deep midwicket for one
short of a length, angling in, played back to him
pushed across him wide, runs off the outer half of the bat for two
into the pads, and he gets off the mark with a single to long-on
quick and full, pushed to short straight cover

and Jadeja strikes. Just enough turn. Prabh jumps out of the crease to go straight, the ball turns away ever so slightly with a puff of dust, and he is miles outside the crease when Dhoni collects the ball. Dhoni pauses a milli-second, the crowd goes berserk, and then he stumps Prabh
premeditates a sweep, wastes a wide delivery, gets just the single
looks to walk at him and play the pick-up shot. Is beaten and hit on the body
on a length, pushed straight of point for one
this one sits in the surface as Taide backs away. Ends up hitting it back to Moeen
shuffles across early, dances down the wicket again, gets a thick inside edge to deep square leg for one
looks to turn this to leg, gets a soft leading edge back to him
dances down the wicket, is nowhere near the pitch of the ball, but uses all his momentum and muscle to loft it over wide long-on for six
flat offbreak, bunted into the gap between deep square and deep midwicket for two
into the pads, worked to deep midwicket for one
down the wicket again, gets the single to long-on
into the pads again, this time he stays with a single
he shows his the reverse sweep early, and Jadeja fires in a length ball, and he switches his grip to switch-hit this over point for four
shimmies down the wicket to push this to long-on for one
on a length, turning in, can't get it past short straight midwicket
yorker at 105ks to end the powerplay. Prabh digs it out
fired into the pads, nudged to deep square leg
again looks for the big sweep, and again he is lucky. The top edge doesn't carry to short fine leg this time
carrom ball, no turn, pushed down to long-off for one
on a length, middle and leg, pushed to long-on for one
shuffles across, then backs away, creates room, and drills this full ball through extra cover for four
short of a length, outside off, punched away to deep point for one
short of a length, wide, cut away, and deep third has moved to deep point to keep them down to one
this one has seamed away a touch? Beats him on the outside edge. On a length, just outside off, and beats his drive

flashing blade of Taide as he gets some width. Pathirana goes to his left from deep third, puts in a dive, but can't field it cleanly. Another team-mate tidies up, and it is poor running from PBKS: they take just two

that is unfortunate for Dhawan. He has got the width, there is no deep third, Dhawan is looking to late-cut it, but it takes a bit of a top edge straight to short third. Actually fair play, Deshpande, it is a cross-seam delivery that has bounced a touch extra
on a length, angling across, driven on the up, and between extra cover and cover. PBKS doing what is needed in the powerplay. Their fastest fifty this IPL
fortune favour Prabh. Tries the big sweep, gets a top edge, and it sails over short fine
on a length, just outside off, pushed wide of cover for one
looks like this is the offbreak, just short of a length, and he has cut it past point. Gaikwad gives chase from inside the circle. Dhawan has overestimated his timing, and takes only two
quick length ball, beats Dhawan's cut. Half a shout for the catch but no edge. Carrom ball again
into the pads, nudged away for a single
on a length, wicket to wicket, carrom ball, and Prabh just chips it back over his head for four. The new ball is skidding on nicely
slower ball, but full toss on the pads, Dhawan doesn't get all of it, but he has managed to place it square of the sweeper on the leg side. Gets four for it
shuffles across this time, Akash bowls the slower one, nearly a yorker, Dhawan digs it out into the leg side for two
Dhawan backs away early, Akash follows him all the way, and then Dhawan changes his shot to play the pick-up over long leg for a six. That is the longer boundary
that should he a wide. Too high as Akash goes for another bouncer
attempted bouncer, wide outside off, slapped down to mid-off
short of a length, skiddy, gets him int he midriff as he looks to pull
short, wide, cut away to deep point for one
looking for a ramp, Deshpande goes wide, Dhawan then tries the reverse ramp, but makes no connection
down the wicket again, Deshpande follows him, beats him, but goes for the leg-bye
jumps down the track, Deshpande shortens the length, Prabh beaten on the slash
this time Deshpande gives him a leg-side half-volley. That's Prabh's zone. Flicks it powerfully for a flat six over square leg
big swing and a miss. Looking to go over midwicket from outside off. Beaten
wide length ball, has a big go at it, gets a thick edge that falls short of deep third. Theekshana does really well to both attack it and still get his body behind it when it falls short
short of a length, angling away, pushed wide of mid-off for one

short of a length, Dhawan down the wicket, gets an inside edge on the pad, and keeps running. Akash fields the ball with time tom spare, Prabh is struggling, but he doesn't flick the throw quickly enough. Misses anyway
the right line and length. Middle and off, slight shape away, and Dhawan has to defend even though he is charging at the bowler
expertly placed. There is a slip in place, but he knows there is no deep third. He late-cuts this deliberately in the air, and clears the slip
sign of things to come? Dhawan dances down first ball, stays away from a length ball, and crashes it over cover for four
looks for swing, tucked away off the pads for one
